recent_posts.title: Build AI Research Agent with Python & Temporal
recent_posts.summary: A step-by-step tutorial on building an AI deep research agent using Python and the OpenAI API, then making it fault-tolerant and observable by integrating Temporal as the workflow orchestration layer. The agent architecture includes multiple specialized sub-agents: triage, clarification, planning, search, and writer agents. Adding Temporal provides full observability into every workflow step and ensures the agent survives crashes or failures.

recent_posts.title: Deep Research AI Agents: From Query to Report  #ai  #programming
recent_posts.summary: A walkthrough of a multi-agent pipeline for deep research tasks. A triage agent evaluates incoming queries for specificity, routing vague ones to a clarifying agent and specific ones to a planner agent. The planner delegates to a search agent that runs concurrent searches, then passes results to a writer agent that synthesizes everything into a final report. A brief code pattern shows how to define individual agents with a name, instructions, and model, executed via a runner.

recent_posts.title: Fixed Flows for AI Agents: Build Reliable, Compliant Workflows with Temporal
Pause Workflows Indefinitely with Temporal  #ai
recent_posts.summary: Temporal enables workflows to pause indefinitely — hours, days, or weeks — without consuming resources. Unlike traditional server setups that require blocking requests, burning resources, or building fragile state machines, Temporal durably persists workflow state and resumes exactly where it left off when input arrives. This is demonstrated through an AI research workflow that waits for user queries and clarification answers with no polling loops or mysterious timeouts.

recent_posts.title: Making LLM calls durable with Temporal and OpenAI Agents
recent_posts.summary: Demonstrates how to use Temporal with the OpenAI Agents plugin to make LLM calls durable and retriable. Covers configuring timeout and retry policies (start-to-close timeout, backoff coefficient, max attempts), connecting a Temporal client, setting up a worker with a task queue, and replacing an in-memory state manager with Temporal for persistent workflow state.

recent_posts.title: Human in the Loop for Deep Research  #ai
recent_posts.summary: A walkthrough of a human-in-the-loop pattern for deep research workflows, where the system pauses execution at key points waiting for user input — such as research initialization and clarification answers — without polling, background schedulers, or fragile state machines. The workflow simply suspends and resumes exactly when conditions are met.

recent_posts.title: Making LLM apps durable with Temporal workflows
recent_posts.summary: Building reliable LLM applications requires more than just orchestrating API calls. Using Temporal, you can wrap an LLM manager in a durable workflow that persists state across restarts, waits indefinitely for human input without consuming resources, and resumes exactly where it left off after failures. The key insight is that plain Python LLM manager code gains durability simply by running inside a Temporal workflow context, where an OpenAI agents plugin intercepts calls and executes them as durable activities — no manual retry logic, checkpointing, or crash recovery code needed.

recent_posts.title: Production Tuning for Temporal Workers at Scale
recent_posts.summary: A webinar covering how to tune and scale temporal workers in production. Marcus and Sam from temporal explain the core concepts of durable execution, how workers poll task queues and use sticky caching for performance, and then walk through the three main tuning knobs: compute (executor slots), memory (sticky workflow cache), and IO (task pollers). Key advice includes applying the theory of constraints to identify bottlenecks before scaling, since blindly adding workers can worsen problems like downstream API rate limits. Language-specific considerations are noted for Java (max workflow thread count) and TypeScript (V8 sandbox options).

recent_posts.title: OpenAI Agents SDK is more durable with Temporal  #ai #openai
recent_posts.summary: The OpenAI Agents SDK integrates with Temporal via a dedicated plugin, enabling durable execution of AI agent workflows. Without this plugin, any failure during a web request to an OpenAI agent results in lost progress requiring a full restart. With the Temporal plugin, workflows gain automatic retries, failure replay from the exact point of failure, and the ability to code only for the happy path while Temporal handles all error scenarios automatically.

recent_posts.title: Avoid duplicate LLM calls with Temporal #llm #coding
recent_posts.summary: Demonstrates how Temporal can prevent duplicate LLM calls when a worker goes down mid-workflow. By leveraging Temporal's durable execution, a workflow resumes exactly where it left off after a worker restart, avoiding redundant LLM calls that waste time and money during long-running tasks like deep research.

top_posts.title: Simplifying Context Engineering for AI Agents in Production
top_posts.summary: Context engineering extends prompt engineering by managing what information AI agents receive throughout their execution. The webinar demonstrates three key challenges: agents handling too many tasks become unpredictable, agents receiving excessive or conflicting context produce hallucinations, and growing conversation histories slow performance. Solutions include scoping agents to single tasks using microagent architecture, loading only relevant context through activities and tools, and pruning conversation history through summarization. Temporal workflows provide durability, orchestration, and isolation for managing agent context in production systems.

top_posts.title: Building long-running interactive MCP tools with Temporal
top_posts.summary: Demonstrates how to build long-running, interactive AI tools using Temporal workflows and Anthropic's Model Context Protocol (MCP). The approach enables durable AI agents that can handle multi-step processes requiring human approval, with tools for triggering workflows, checking status, and sending approval signals. Features an invoice processing example that showcases human-in-the-loop functionality, where AI agents can start processes, wait for human input, and continue execution reliably over extended periods.

top_posts.title: Tips for running Temporal on Kubernetes
top_posts.summary: Temporal provides durability as a service for distributed applications, handling state persistence, retries, and recovery automatically. Deploy Temporal on Kubernetes using official Helm charts, but disable bundled dependencies and connect to external production databases. Workers should be containerized with both workflow definitions and worker processes together, deployed as standard Kubernetes deployments. For autoscaling, avoid CPU/memory metrics and instead use Task Queue backlog, schedule-to-start latency, and worker task slot utilization. KEDA enables automatic scaling based on queue depth. Set GOMAXPROCS to match Pod CPU limits to prevent throttling and maintain consistent latency. Load test iteratively on dedicated clusters before production changes.

top_posts.title: Building Enterprise Production-Ready Agentic AI with Grid Dynamics
top_posts.summary: Grid Dynamics and Temporal demonstrate how to build production-ready AI agents using Temporal's workflow orchestration platform. The webinar covers transitioning from AI MVPs to enterprise-grade systems with built-in observability, guard rails, and reliability. Key topics include handling LLM failures, cost management, state tracking, and implementing proper monitoring for AI workflows. The presentation showcases the OpenAI Agents SDK integration with Temporal, emphasizing how orchestration solves common AI deployment challenges like non-deterministic behavior, downtime handling, and scaling issues.

top_posts.title: How Cargo engineers a smarter go-to-market process with Temporal
top_posts.summary: Cargo, a Y Combinator company, built a revenue orchestration platform using Temporal as the core workflow engine to connect fragmented go-to-market tools. They use Temporal for event-driven GTM workflows, data synchronization, and AI workflow orchestration, while migrating from Postgres to ClickHouse for better analytical performance. The engineering-first approach emphasizes durable execution patterns and reliable automation over traditional sales development teams.
